TASK 3: LCA Subtask 3.1: LCA of H /NG Blends for Various End Use Applications – Description 2 The NG pathways considered will include both conventional and shale gas production; gas processing and separation; and gas compression, storage, and transmission/distribution to the H 2 injection point. The H pathways will include all renewable and near-zero-carbon production 2 technology options (e.g., low-temperature electrolysis and high-temperature electrolysis using solar, wind, and nuclear power), as well as H compression, storage, and transmission to the 2 injection point into NG pipelines. The downstream pathway for the H /NG blend will include 2 transmission/distribution, compression via gas reciprocating engines and electric motors, and storage and combustion at-end use applications such as building appliances, industrial boilers, and gas turbines for power generation. ANL will perform LCA to evaluate energy use by type (e.g., fossil, nuclear, renewable), pathway energy efficiency, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions (e.g., carbon dioxide [CO ] and [CH ]), and criteria air pollutant (CAP) emissions (e.g., nitrogen 2 4 oxides [NO ], carbon monoxide, volatile organic compounds, sulfur oxides) for each step in the x technology pathways of the H /NG blend and at a wide range of blending ratios spanning 0%– 2 100% H . 2 17 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. LCA of NG/H Blends for Various End Use Applications – Technology Advance/Outcomes 2 The LCA in this subtask aims to answer the following research questions when comparing with conventional NG pathways: 1. What are the impacts of hydrogen primary energy sources and production technology pathways on life cycle total and fossil energy use and associated emissions? 2. What are the implications of hydrogen storage types, delivery methods, injection pressure, and associated energy use and emissions? 3. What are the impacts of the combustion of H /NGblends on the efficiency and emissions 2 of existing internal combustion engines driving the pipeline compressors? 4. What are the implications of leakage and fugitive emissions of various H /NG blends? 2 5. What are the implications of various blending ratios and end-use applications on GHG and CAP emissions? 6. Are there regional preferences or differences associated with H production, delivery, and 2 storage pathways? 7.
